newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bridgestone to invest in Indonesian, Thai output.
newsitem.headline: Bridgestone to invest in Indonesian, Thai output.

text.p: Japanese tyre maker Bridgestone Corp said on Thursday that it would invest about 27 billion yen to boost production in Indonesia and Thailand.
The investment was needed to cope with growing demand for tyres in Indonesia and Thailand, Bridgestone said.

In Indonesia, Bridgestone plans to invest about 12 billion yen to build a second plant at its unit PT Bridgestone Tire Indonesia, it said in a statement. The plant, to be built in West Java, would start operations in January 1999, it said.
It would be capable of producing about 20 tonnes of passenger car and small truck tyres a day, rising to about 50 tonnes a day by the end of 2001, it said.

The capacity of the unit's first plant, which makes various types of tyres, would also rise to 140 tonnes a day by the end of 1997 from 120 tonnes at the end of 1996, Bridgestone said, but it did not immediately say how much it would invest in the first plant.

In Thailand, Bridgestone plans to invest about 15 billion yen to expand two plants at its Thai unit, Thai Bridgestone Co Ltd, near Bangkok. The first plant's capacity was expected to increase to 145 tonnes of tyres a day by the end of 1998, up from 135 tonnes a day at the end of 1996, the company said.
The second plant would be capable of producing 80 tonnes of tyres a day by the end of 1998, up from 38 tonnes daily at the end of 1996, it said.
